The unit suite asserts the classes, the transitions and the reading rule (`scripts/picker-feedback.test.mjs`); only a frame of the running app shows the ground and the edge the row actually paints inside a dialog whose own ground is `elevated`, and what the user is left with when the answer arrives after the dialog is gone. The transcript note count is measured either side of the U2 case — 1 before the click, 2 after it, with the dialog closed 80 ms in — because the refusal sentence is identical for every refused pick and only a count can prove a second one was written. The U7 pair is measured rather than described: between the two frames AE is 85,307 px (1.77%) of 4,813,440, of which 13,230 px (2% fuzz) sit in one 952x64 band across the header sentence's own text line and 274 px are the clock.

The backend and the dev server are committed beside these frames in harness/ (serve-gate.py, ask-gate.vite.mjs); they used to be a scratch rig under /tmp that nobody else could run.
why: WHAT THESE FRAMES ARE. before-click/localOperatorDark.webp is the real pending ask gate in the shipped renderer - three bordered option buttons, the Recommended mark beside the label, the hint - rather than a story fixture. It is the only live frame of the card in this tree.

WHAT THEY ARE NOT, and this is the correction the QA round asked for. after-click/localOperatorDark.webp is NOT a picture of the gate resolving, and it is renamed after-click-unresolved/ so the path says so. The Vite dev server died between the two frames (a second status write on a committed response, ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT, from scripts/vite-plugins/desktop-proxy.ts - fixed in this round), so that frame shows the gate still on screen with three failure surfaces instead of a cleared card. click-result.json's own `after` block reports {"found": true, "count": 3}: the DOM had not cleared, and the record says so.

The click ITSELF is recorded, not photographed: click-result.json carries the pre-click DOM, the aim point after elementFromPoint confirmed those pixels resolve to that option (so the control is hit-testable, not merely painted), and the post-click DOM. owner-answer.json is the owner's own return value, {"PAIRING": ["Popup is not open"]} - the label of a NON-first option after the harness rotated `recommended: 1` to the front, so it cannot be an index-0 accident. Its `names` field is textContent and INCLUDES the aria-hidden ordinal ("2.Popup is not open..."); the claim that the accessible name is the label rests on `ordinalHidden: true` plus the aria-hidden markup, not on that field - which is why it is named textContent.

The healthy re-capture of the pair is DEFERRED, not done, and the two frames above are not evidence for the resolution. scripts/click-proof.mjs and the committed rig are what the next round needs; see this directory's README for the exact blocker.
Captured in localOperatorDark only: this is a wire-and-interaction proof, not a palette proof. The twelve-theme question is answered by chat-ask-options/, which the sweep takes across every palette.
